question: I control a permanent with the ability '{T}: Add {G} for each creature you control,' but right now I control no creatures, so tapping it would add no mana at all. Is that still a mana ability, or does it become a regular activated ability that has to use the stack once it can't actually produce mana?

expected.shortAnswer: Yes: it stays a mana ability even when it would add no mana.
expected.answer: A permanent has an ability that reads “{T}: Add {G} for each creature you control.” The ability is still a mana ability even if you control no creatures or if the permanent is already tapped.

whyHard: Players expect whether an ability "counts" as a mana ability to depend on the current game state -- if it can't actually produce mana right now, surely it must use the stack like any other ability. The definition is fixed at the ability's text, not its momentary output: it never uses the stack, win or lose, whether or not it can currently produce mana.
